result:
I could not fully verify any of the three answers, so this judgment is partial.

**Solution 2 (∞) is wrong.** Its key claim is that the vector fields a(y₁₂,y₁₃)∂_{y₁₂} + b(y₁₂,y₁₃)∂_{y₁₃} commute with the left-invariant generators of D. In exponential coordinates the generator e₁ has a ∂_{w₁₂} component of the form (x₂/2)∂_{w₁₂}, so [X, e₁] contains the term (x₂/2)·∂a/∂y₁₂ ∂_{w₁₂}. Since D is spanned by e₁, e₂, e₃ and has no ∂_{x}-components in the commutator, this term cannot be absorbed, so X does not preserve D unless ∂a/∂y₁₂ = 0. The infinite-dimensionality argument therefore fails.

**Solution 3 (21) is unsupported.** It identifies a candidate model (B₃/P₁,₂ of dimension 8) without checking that its grading is the (3,3,2) symbol of a (3,6,8) distribution. Its own recollections are explicitly uncertain. It is not a verified derivation.

**Solution 1 (29) is the most substantive.** It sets up the symbol via pencils in sl(3), gives an explicit symbol and realization, and reports graded prolongation dimensions that are internally consistent: the degree −3, −2, −1 dimensions (2, 3, 3) match the symbol, and the total 8 + 7 + 6 + 3 + 3 + 2 = 29 adds up. I did not check the prolongation computation or the claim that this pencil gives the maximum, so 29 is plausible but not confirmed.

Since Solution 2 is shown to be wrong and Solution 3 is weakly supported, Solution 1 is the best candidate, though it is not verified.

CHOICE: 1
